statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and seven of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the seventeen slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 10 and 14, all far below the block threshold. Stress is 38, moderate: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods is in force, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar response to 8 September, a Monday US Treasury press conference on isolating Iran's economy is scheduled, the 30-year yield sits near a two-decade high around 5.27% after the buyback rally faded, and crude has closed a second consecutive week higher. Confidence is 85, high: the Friday close, VIX, H.15 yields, WTI and the seven-day calendar were re-verified against primary sources this hour, and a conflicting third-party index quote was resolved against corroborating sources, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to observe.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, while the VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.0% and near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with application and infrastructure software up about 1.2% against a semiconductor group averaging roughly -0.7%, and megacaps five up against three down. Cross-asset context stays in conflict: the long end sold off while the VIX fell and gold rose, which is a Stress and Confidence signature rather than the aligned amplifier stack that would justify a higher Tail. Tail is therefore held at its closed-venue floor for the seven shut hours and in the 10-14 band across the seventeen reopen hours, with the narrow evidence-based danger window placed on the reopen repricing interval from 22:00Z to 02:00Z rather than across the whole overnight session.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with seventeen reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through seven shut hours, then carries conditional readings between 10 and 14 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through a US cash open that now sits inside the window, while a faded Treasury buyback rally, live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a Monday Treasury briefing on isolating Iran and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, which weekly market coverage confirms as 18:00 ET and the clearest scheduled US price-discovery point of the day. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T15:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T14:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the sixteen hours after it sit inside the horizon while the first seven do not, and both the US cash open at 13:30Z and the first full hour after it now fall inside the window. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open. The direction is corroborated by the broad Friday closes, with the S&P 500 at 7,674.37 up 0.43%, the Dow at 53,277.01 up 0.98% and the Nasdaq Composite at 26,180.46 up 0.43%, while every major index still lost ground on the week and the Nasdaq Composite fell about 2%. One third-party index quote page again returned a level and a negative daily change inconsistent with those closes and carried its own delayed-data warning; it was discarded. The VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%, in a 14.77-15.95 range. Rates remain the loudest cross-asset channel: H.15 for 20 August shows the 2-year at 4.19%, the 5-year at 4.39%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, and Friday's close put the 10-year at 4.73% and the 30-year at 5.27%, near a two-decade high, after the Treasury buyback announcement produced a rally that faded within two sessions. WTI closed at 87.06, up 0.26% on the day and higher for a second consecutive week, with Iran-related supply risk and a renewed Houthi threat to Saudi Red Sea export logistics in the background; the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since late February, so it is a standing condition rather than a new discontinuity, and the US-Iran memorandum of understanding lapsed on 17 August without an extension. Three policy items are unpriced by any equity venue over the weekend: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods now in force, Canada's dollar-for-dollar retaliation dated 8 September, and a Monday US Treasury press conference set to detail an economic-isolation plan for Iran. Shared Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 15:07Z and labelled delayed latest-session data, is consistent with conflict rather than an aligned one-way regime: index futures modestly higher on the session, VIX futures lower, crude marginally higher, gold up 2.39%, Treasury futures lower across the curve and the semiconductor group negative against firm software. That raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The week ahead is dense: Nvidia reports on Wednesday after the close with results due about 20:20Z and the call at 21:00Z, the July PCE report and the second GDP estimate land the same morning, and the Jackson Hole symposium runs from Thursday with the Fed Chair keynote on Friday. Those are checkpoints inside the top-level event calendar, not observed structure, and they do not move Tail before they print.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available, while the 21:00Z clock-hour on 22 August and the 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z clock-hours on 23 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress decayed across the shut weekend, from 42 at the start of the window on Saturday afternoon down to 34 by Sunday morning, then turned back up to 37 by the most recent published hour as the Sunday reopen came into view. Confidence held between 85 and 87, easing only as the last observed cash session receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The following six slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress rises from 38 to 46 as the reopen approaches with the weekend information set unpriced. The final seventeen slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12 and the first full hour after it 13, after which Tail decays through the Asian session to 10 as the modelled danger window closes at 02:00Z. From the European open the conditional readings rebuild through 11 and 12 as cross-asset alignment first becomes readable, reaching 13 across the US pre-market and a horizon peak of 14 in the two closing slots, which contain the US cash open at 13:30Z and the first full hour after it. Every one of those readings is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and all 24 map to EA_ON.
